skills.title: SwiftUI engineering entry point
skills.summary: Build, review, or repair a SwiftUI feature. Start here for native UI semantics, task scoping, SDK verification, and selecting focused Apple-platform skills.
skills.limits: Task scoping and native semantics across Apple platforms; this entry point is not an exhaustive API or HIG index.

skills.title: State, identity, and architecture
skills.summary: Fix SwiftUI state ownership, Observation, bindings, environment injection, view identity, scene scope, and testable feature boundaries without imposing an architecture.
skills.limits: Ownership and identity patterns; executable core and selected SwiftUI examples do not cover every platform observation lifecycle.

skills.title: Concurrency and lifecycle
skills.summary: Design or repair Swift async/await, actors, Sendable boundaries, cancellation, task ownership, stale results, continuations, and Swift 6 migration.
skills.limits: Isolation, cancellation, and stale-result patterns with controlled async examples; no general concurrency verifier or workload benchmark.

skills.title: Navigation and presentation
skills.summary: Build or fix SwiftUI NavigationStack, NavigationSplitView, tabs, sheets, deep links, route restoration, and scene-specific selection.
skills.limits: Typed routes, presentation, restoration, and scene ownership; platform navigation journeys require their own runtime evidence.

skills.title: Adaptive layout and scrolling
skills.summary: Repair SwiftUI layout, safe areas, stacks, grids, lists, scrolling, custom Layout, GeometryReader, Dynamic Type, and right-to-left adaptation.
skills.limits: Layout diagnosis and risky-size checks; no exhaustive device, locale, keyboard, or window-size screenshot matrix.

skills.title: Controls, forms, and input
skills.summary: Implement SwiftUI buttons, menus, pickers, forms, focus, keyboard submission, text entry, gestures, drag and drop, and validation with native semantics.
skills.limits: Control and commit semantics; IME, keyboard, pointer, and assistive interactions need destination-specific execution.

skills.title: Accessibility and localization
skills.summary: Audit or implement VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, accessible controls, contrast, Reduce Motion, keyboard access, localization, and right-to-left SwiftUI behavior.
skills.limits: Accessibility workflows and failure probes; static inspection and automated audits do not certify assistive-technology journeys.

skills.title: Visual language, materials, and motion
skills.summary: Refine SwiftUI hierarchy, typography, color, SF Symbols, materials, Liquid Glass, animation, charts, and consistent native-feeling components using Apple HIG principles.
skills.limits: Hierarchy, repeated surfaces, optional themes, and materials; palettes and runtime rendering remain product-specific.

skills.title: Persistence, drafts, and synchronization
skills.summary: Design or repair SwiftData, Core Data, file storage, migrations, save/cancel semantics, local-first data, CloudKit synchronization, and durable operation identity.
skills.limits: Drafts, value authority, local persistence, migration and sync boundaries; SwiftData examples do not prove disk recovery or CloudKit behavior.

skills.title: Networking, caching, and remote state
skills.summary: Implement or audit URLSession clients, authentication, retries, cancellation, pagination, image loading, caching, and truthful offline SwiftUI state.
skills.limits: Client response, retry, identity, and cache contracts; not a backend implementation or production delivery guarantee.

skills.title: Behavior tests, previews, and evidence
skills.summary: Design Swift Testing, XCTest, UI automation, preview fixtures, accessibility checks, and deterministic regression tests for SwiftUI features.
skills.limits: Test design and evidence classification; example tests and evaluation contracts are distinct from completed agent evaluations.

skills.title: Platform-native scenes and interaction
skills.summary: Adapt SwiftUI apps for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS with appropriate scenes, navigation, input, windows, focus, and lifecycle.
skills.limits: Platform decision guidance; framework availability and actual focus, window, spatial, or watch interactions need separate verification.

skills.title: UIKit and AppKit interoperability
skills.summary: Bridge SwiftUI with UIKit or AppKit using representables, hosting, coordinators, delegates, text systems, and explicit lifecycle ownership.
skills.limits: Representable lifecycle and ownership patterns; specialized text, media, and graphics bridges need focused implementation and tests.

skills.title: System surfaces and framework integration
skills.summary: Integrate WidgetKit, App Intents, ActivityKit, notifications, Spotlight, WatchConnectivity, HealthKit, and StoreKit through truthful shared commands and projections.
skills.limits: Boundary and failure-mode playbooks for eight frameworks; specialized domain algorithms, backend receipt systems, and exhaustive API catalogs remain out of scope.

skills.title: Apple project governance
skills.summary: Create, repair, or audit Xcode and Swift package configuration. Use for targets, schemes, resources, generated projects, entitlements, build settings, and configuration drift.
skills.limits: Project ownership and artifact inspection; signing, capabilities, and generated state must be checked for the actual product graph.

skills.title: Apple privacy and integration safety
skills.summary: Design or audit protected-data access and system boundaries. Use for permissions, purpose strings, privacy manifests, data minimization, retention, deletion, disclosures, and account changes.
skills.limits: Data-flow and permission boundary review; neither legal certification nor proof of live protected-data behavior.

skills.title: Apple performance and behavior-preserving cleanup
skills.summary: Diagnose or improve SwiftUI responsiveness, startup, memory, energy, and hot paths. Use measurements and explicit behavior contracts before optimization or broad compaction.
skills.limits: Measurement and behavior-preserving cleanup workflows; no speed, energy, or memory improvement is implied without a comparable workload.

skills.title: Apple runtime and device validation
skills.summary: Build, install, run, render, and validate Apple apps on the correct destination. Use for simulator/device evidence, screenshots, hardware, paired devices, and infrastructure triage.
skills.limits: Claim-specific runtime proof and screen-review inventory; artifacts from one environment do not cover untested hardware or services.

skills.title: App Store readiness
skills.summary: Plan, audit, or prepare an App Store candidate. Use for release scope, storefront metadata, privacy disclosures, review access, TestFlight, and explicit submission or release gates.
skills.limits: Candidate, authority, and release-ledger reconciliation; account service state and current submission rules require live verification.

skills.title: macOS productization and distribution
skills.summary: Prepare or inspect a macOS distribution artifact. Use for Developer ID or Mac App Store signing, hardened runtime, notarization, packaging, Gatekeeper, installation, and update integrity.
skills.limits: macOS distribution and trust workflow; local compilation does not establish notarization or downloaded-install behavior.

skills.title: Swift API design and dependency boundaries
skills.summary: Write or review Swift APIs, value models, dependency injection, error contracts, access control, formatting, and language-version migrations without imposing an app architecture.
skills.limits: API design and dependency-boundary guidance; not a complete Swift language manual or a mandatory architecture.

skills.title: Reproducible Apple build and debug workflows
skills.summary: Create or repair reproducible Xcode and SwiftPM build, test, debug, and simulator workflows with explicit destinations, raw logs, safe tooling, and truthful evidence.
skills.limits: Reproducible build/test plans with a tested command wrapper; actual schemes, destinations, signing, and debugger behavior require Xcode execution.

skills.title: Evidence-based Xcode build optimization
skills.summary: Benchmark and improve Xcode clean, no-change, and edit-build latency; analyze compiler hotspots, script phases, target graphs, SwiftPM plugins, and measured rollback decisions.
skills.limits: Six diagnostic and measurement tracks with descriptive statistics; no project-specific speedup or critical path is inferred automatically.

skills.title: SwiftData schemas, queries, and migrations
skills.summary: Design and repair SwiftData models, relationships, predicates, contexts, disk-backed migrations, indexes, history, and CloudKit-compatible schema evolution.
skills.limits: Schema, query, context, and migration guidance; existing in-memory examples do not establish disk upgrades, history processing, or CloudKit convergence.

skills.title: Core Data confinement, history, and migration
skills.summary: Diagnose Core Data contexts, managed object identity, fetches, batch changes, persistent history, SQLite migrations, merge policies, and CloudKit mirroring.
skills.limits: Context, batch, history, and migration decision guidance; this revision adds no executable Core Data migration or mirroring fixture.

skills.title: App Intents, entities, and system actions
skills.summary: Implement App Intents, App Entities, entity queries, App Shortcuts, and system actions with shared commands, authorization, process isolation, and runtime registration evidence.
skills.limits: Entity, authorization, and invocation contracts; system registration, discoverability, and actual Siri/Shortcuts execution remain destination-specific.

skills.title: Privacy-safe logs and performance diagnostics
skills.summary: Instrument and diagnose Apple apps using unified logging, signposts, Instruments traces, crash symbolication, memory graphs, and reproducible evidence without leaking user data.
skills.limits: Privacy-safe diagnostic workflows; no captured trace, symbolication result, or leak-free claim is supplied by the guidance alone.

skills.title: Background execution and resumable work
skills.summary: Design Apple background refresh, processing, background transfers, and expiration-safe work with durable progress, bounded execution, and truthful scheduling state.
skills.limits: Expiration and recovery contracts across applicable mechanisms; no exact scheduling guarantee or live background-delivery proof.

skills.title: Apple app trust boundaries and secure data
skills.summary: Review Apple app credentials, Keychain use, transport trust, deep links, untrusted input, sandbox boundaries, dependencies, and secure failure handling.
skills.limits: Trust-boundary guidance and a narrow tested route parser; parsing does not authorize access or replace a full application security review.
